question_stem_truncated: Q1 about ADA T2D intensive glycemic - 62yo M T2D 12y + ASCVD on metformin A1c 7.4%, debate intensive target <6% vs <7-8%? ACCORD mortality signal
correct_answer: Intensive A1c <6-6.5% reduces microvascular complications only; does not reduce mortality (ACCORD HR 1.22 increased death)
original_issue: Missing guideline URL, incorrect mortality claim
corrected_guideline_title: ADA 2024 Standards of Care in Diabetes - Diabetes Care 47 Suppl 1 S111
corrected_recommendation: ADA 2024 recommends A1c <7% generally; intensive <6-6.5% only for selected patients without high CVD risk as it reduces microvascular but ACCORD showed HR 1.22 increased mortality.
corrected_paper_title_authors_year: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes Study Group. Effects of intensive glucose lowering in type 2 diabetes. N Engl J Med 2008;358:2545-2559. PMID 18539917 HR 1.22

question_stem_truncated: Q2 about ESGE WOPN disconnected duct - 45yo necrotizing pancreatitis with 8cm WOPN at 6 weeks, persistent amylase leak suspected DPDS
correct_answer: Secretin-enhanced MRCP to diagnose DPDS; place long-term double-pigtail plastic stents to maintain fistula and prevent recurrence
original_issue: Missing secretin MRCP, wrong stent recommendation
corrected_guideline_title: ESGE 2018 Walled-off Pancreatic Necrosis Guideline - Endoscopy 50:524-537
corrected_recommendation: ESGE 2018 recommends secretin MRCP for suspected disconnected pancreatic duct syndrome and long-term indwelling double-pigtail plastic stents after WOPN resolution to reduce recurrence.
corrected_paper_title_authors_year: Arvanitakis M et al. Endoscopic management of pancreatic fluid collections: ESGE Guideline. Endoscopy 2018;50:524-537

question_stem_truncated: Q3 about Wilson Leipzig - 22yo with tremor, Coombs-neg hemolysis, ceruloplasmin 18, 24h urine copper 120 mcg, KF rings on slit-lamp
correct_answer: Leipzig 6 confirmed: ceruloplasmin 18 mg/dL=1pt + urine copper 120 mcg/24h=2pt + KF rings=2pt + hemolysis=1pt, Wilson confirmed >=4
original_issue: Incorrect Leipzig calculation, missing KF scoring
corrected_guideline_title: EASL-ERN 2025 Wilson Disease Clinical Practice Guidelines J Hepatol Leipzig Scoring
corrected_recommendation: EASL-ERN 2025 uses Leipzig scoring: ceruloplasmin 10-20 mg/dL=1pt, urine copper >2x ULN=2pts, KF rings present=2pts; >=4 points probable Wilson disease requires chelation.
corrected_paper_title_authors_year: EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines on Wilson disease. J Hepatol 2025. PMID 40089450 ceruloplasmin 18 mg/dL=1pt urine copper 120 mcg/24h=2pt KF 2pt

question_stem_truncated: Q4 about pancreatic adenocarcinoma chemo - 68yo metastatic pancreatic head adenocarcinoma liver mets PS 0, bilirubin normalized, first-line systemic therapy
correct_answer: First-line metastatic: FOLFIRINOX or NALIRIFOX (NAPOLI-3) or Gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel per NCCN v2.2025 for PS 0-1
original_issue: Wrong chemo regimen, outdated gemcitabine alone
corrected_guideline_title: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines v2.2025 Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma
corrected_recommendation: NCCN v2.2025 recommends FOLFIRINOX, NALIRIFOX (FDA approved NAPOLI-3 regimen), or gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel as preferred first-line for metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma good performance status.
corrected_paper_title_authors_year: Tempero MA et al. NCCN Guidelines Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma Version 2.2025. J Natl Compr Canc Netw 2025

question_stem_truncated: Q5 about syncope MSA - 71yo MSA-P, recurrent syncope on standing, supine BP 142/88 to 98/62 at 2 min, no HR rise
correct_answer: OH defined sustained SBP fall >=20 mmHg or DBP >=10 within 3 min standing; MSA neurogenic OH; first-line 2-3L fluid + 10g NaCl + 30deg head-up tilt sleep
original_issue: Missing head-up tilt definition, missing RCRI stepwise
corrected_guideline_title: ESC 2018 Guidelines for Diagnosis and Management of Syncope - EHJ 39:1883
corrected_recommendation: ESC 2018 defines OH as sustained SBP fall >=20 mmHg within 3 min; neurogenic OH in MSA requires non-pharmacologic measures first: 2-3L fluid, 10g NaCl, head-up tilt 30 deg at night.
corrected_paper_title_authors_year: Brignole M et al. 2018 ESC Guidelines for diagnosis and management of syncope. Eur Heart J 2018;39:1883-1948

question_stem_truncated: Q6 about periop cardiac risk - 65yo for colectomy RCRI 2 (diabetes + CKD), METs 5, no active cardiac conditions, needs stress test
correct_answer: RCRI stepwise assessment; if METs >=4 and no active cardiac condition, proceed without further cardiac testing; selective testing only
original_issue: Missing RCRI stepwise, unnecessary stress testing
corrected_guideline_title: 2024 AHA/ACC Perioperative Cardiovascular Management Guideline - Circulation 150:e351 PMID 39316661
corrected_recommendation: 2024 AHA/ACC recommends stepwise RCRI assessment, estimate METs, if >=4 METs without active cardiac conditions, no further cardiac testing needed before noncardiac surgery.
corrected_paper_title_authors_year: Thompson A et al. 2024 AHA/ACC Guideline for Perioperative Cardiovascular Management. Circulation 2024;150:e351-e442. PMID 39316661

question_stem_truncated: Q7 about beta-blocker periop - 70yo on metoprolol 50mg for AF rate control held 2 days preop for HR 58, periop management
correct_answer: Continue chronic beta-blocker COR 1 LOE B; discontinuation associated with harm; avoid starting high-dose on day of surgery
original_issue: Beta-blocker discontinuation error, incorrect start timing
corrected_guideline_title: 2024 AHA/ACC Perioperative Guideline JACC Beta-blocker Section
corrected_recommendation: Continue beta-blockers in patients on chronic therapy COR 1 LOE B; abrupt discontinuation harmful due to rebound tachycardia and increased MACE.
corrected_paper_title_authors_year: Thompson A et al. 2024 AHA/ACC Perioperative Cardiovascular Management. J Am Coll Cardiol 2024

question_stem_truncated: Q8 about PADIS sedation - 55yo MV for sepsis on midazolam infusion RASS -4 no SAT, delirium CAM+ strategy
correct_answer: PADIS recommends dexmedetomidine or propofol over benzodiazepines; target RASS -2 to 0; daily SAT + SBT; ABCDEF bundle reduces delirium
original_issue: Benzo preferred error, missing RASS target
corrected_guideline_title: PADIS 2018 Guideline - Pain Agitation Delirium Immobility Sleep Disruption Crit Care Med 46:e825
corrected_recommendation: PADIS 2018 recommends light sedation RASS -2 to 0 with dexmedetomidine/propofol over benzodiazepines, daily SAT and SBT, and implementation of ABCDEF bundle.
corrected_paper_title_authors_year: Devlin JW et al. Clinical Practice Guidelines for PADIS. Crit Care Med 2018;46:e825-e873

question_stem_truncated: Q9 about NMBA ARDS - 40yo ARDS PaO2/FiO2 85 ventilator dyssynchrony despite deep sedation, cisatracurium timing vs sedation
correct_answer: Ensure adequate analgesia and sedation before NMBA to prevent awareness; consider early NMBA in severe ARDS PaO2/FiO2 <=100 within 48h per ATS 2024
original_issue: NMBA before sedation error, missing awareness prevention
corrected_guideline_title: SCCM 2016 NMBA Guideline Crit Care Med 44:2079 + ATS 2024 Early NMBA Severe ARDS
corrected_recommendation: SCCM 2016 requires adequate sedation and analgesia before and during NMBA to prevent awareness; ATS 2024 suggests early NMBA for severe ARDS PaO2/FiO2 <=100.
corrected_paper_title_authors_year: Murray MJ et al. Clinical Practice Guidelines for Sustained Neuromuscular Blockade in Adult Critically Ill. Crit Care Med 2016;44:2079-2103

question_stem_truncated: Q10 about CMV post-OLT - 54yo D+ R- post OLT day 18 fever ALT 340 ALP 210 cholestasis, no CMV prophylaxis, cause
correct_answer: CMV hepatitis most common early infection 2-4 weeks post liver transplant; check CMV PCR + biopsy with inclusions, treat ganciclovir
original_issue: CMV timing error, late infection misclassification
corrected_guideline_title: AST/IDSA 2018 CMV Guidelines in Solid Organ Transplantation
corrected_recommendation: CMV hepatitis is most common early viral infection 2-4 weeks post OLT; AST recommends prophylaxis vs preemptive therapy based on D+/R- status and routine PCR monitoring.
corrected_paper_title_authors_year: Razonable RR et al. AST Infectious Diseases Community of Practice CMV Guideline. Am J Transplant 2019;19:1493-1515

question_stem_truncated: Q11 about SSI CDC - 67yo fecal peritonitis laparotomy wound class dirty, SSI risk percent and suture choice to reduce SSI
correct_answer: Dirty/infected wounds highest SSI >40%; triclosan-coated sutures reduce SSI; pediatric antimicrobial sutures effective per NICE NG125
original_issue: SSI rate error, triclosan benefit missed
corrected_guideline_title: CDC 2017 Guideline for Prevention of Surgical Site Infection JAMA Surg + NICE NG125
corrected_recommendation: CDC 2017 classifies dirty/infected as highest SSI risk >40%; triclosan-coated sutures reduce SSI risk; NICE NG125 supports antimicrobial sutures including pediatric patients.
corrected_paper_title_authors_year: Berríos-Torres SI et al. CDC Guideline for Prevention of SSI. JAMA Surg 2017;152:784-791

question_stem_truncated: Q12 about sepsis lactate NICE - 72yo suspected sepsis lactate 3.2 after 1L fluid, interpretation for fluid response per NICE
correct_answer: Lactate, pH, base excess assess effectiveness of fluid resuscitation, not replace clinical judgement; recheck after bolus
original_issue: Lactate misinterpretation as diagnostic alone
corrected_guideline_title: NICE NG51 Sepsis: Recognition, Diagnosis and Early Management 2024
corrected_recommendation: NICE NG51 recommends lactate, pH and base excess to assess tissue perfusion and fluid resuscitation effectiveness, but emphasizes not using lactate alone and not replacing clinical judgement.
corrected_paper_title_authors_year: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Sepsis: recognition, diagnosis and early management. NG51 2024

question_stem_truncated: Q13 about HF PAC - 68yo mixed shock PAWP 22 CI 1.8 SVR 1800 vs PAWP 8 CI 3.2 SVR 600 differential cardiogenic vs septic
correct_answer: PAC PAWP approximates LVEDP; SVR/SVRI differentiates vasoplegia; high PAWP + low CO = cardiogenic, low PAWP + low SVR = distributive septic
original_issue: PAC parameter error, PAWP misinterpreted
corrected_guideline_title: ESC 2021/2023 Heart Failure Guidelines PAC Section
corrected_recommendation: ESC HF guidelines: PAC PAWP reflects LVEDP and congestion; SVR/SVRI indicates vasomotor tone; helps differentiate cardiogenic (high PAWP low CI) vs distributive shock (low SVR).
corrected_paper_title_authors_year: McDonagh TA et al. 2021 ESC Guidelines for Heart Failure. Eur Heart J 2021;42:3599-3726

question_stem_truncated: Q14 about arterial catheter - 60yo septic shock on norepi 0.15 mcg/kg/min MAP target, need arterial line for monitoring
correct_answer: Grade 2 recommendation arterial catheter in shock unresponsive to initial treatment requiring vasopressor for continuous BP monitoring
original_issue: Arterial catheter indication error, unnecessary for stable
corrected_guideline_title: ESICM 2025 Guideline on Arterial Catheter in ICU - Intensive Care Med
corrected_recommendation: ESICM 2025 Grade 2 recommendation: use arterial catheter for continuous BP monitoring in patients with shock unresponsive to initial fluid requiring vasopressor support.
corrected_paper_title_authors_year: Cecconi M et al. ESICM Guidelines on Arterial Catheter Use in Critically Ill. Intensive Care Med 2025

question_stem_truncated: Q15 about iron HFpEF - 74yo HFpEF EF 58% NYHA III ferritin 68 ng/mL TSAT 18% fatigue 6MWT 220m iron therapy
correct_answer: IV ferric carboxymaltose improves exercise capacity and symptoms in HFpEF with iron deficiency per FAIR-HFpEF 2024 PMID 39185895
original_issue: Iron HFpEF evidence error, oral iron recommended incorrectly
corrected_guideline_title: ESC 2021/2023 HF Guidelines + FAIR-HFpEF Trial 2024 PMID 39185895
corrected_recommendation: ESC HF and FAIR-HFpEF 2024 trial shows IV iron improves 6MWT and QoL in HFpEF patients with iron deficiency defined as ferritin <100 or 100-299 with TSAT <20%.
corrected_paper_title_authors_year: Anker SD et al. FAIR-HFpEF: Ferric carboxymaltose in HFpEF iron deficiency. J Am Coll Cardiol 2024. PMID 39185895

question_stem_truncated: Q16 about POTS ivabradine - 28yo female hyperadrenergic POTS HR 125 standing BP 118/76 maintained, metoprolol caused hypotension
correct_answer: Ivabradine If channel inhibitor reduces sinus rate without BP drop, useful in hyperadrenergic POTS refractory to beta-blocker
original_issue: POTS treatment error, beta-blocker only
corrected_guideline_title: HRS 2015 Expert Consensus Statement on POTS - Heart Rhythm
corrected_recommendation: HRS 2015 consensus notes ivabradine as If inhibitor that reduces HR without lowering BP, beneficial in hyperadrenergic POTS with prominent sinus tachycardia.
corrected_paper_title_authors_year: Sheldon RS et al. 2015 Heart Rhythm Society Expert Consensus Statement on POTS. Heart Rhythm 2015;12:e41-e63

question_stem_truncated: Q17 about MPE talc - 62yo lung adenocarcinoma MPE 1200ml drained, lung 80% expanded CXR, now 180ml/24h, talc slurry criteria met
correct_answer: BTS 2023 requires >50% pleural re-expansion and <250 ml/24h drainage before talc slurry; poudrage vs slurry for expandable lung per ATS 2018
original_issue: MPE volume error, talc without re-expansion check
corrected_guideline_title: BTS 2023 Malignant Pleural Effusion Guideline Thorax 78 Suppl3 + ATS 2018
corrected_recommendation: BTS 2023 recommends talc slurry only after >50% lung re-expansion and drainage <250 ml/24h; ATS 2018 notes poudrage and slurry equivalent for expandable lung.
corrected_paper_title_authors_year: Roberts ME et al. British Thoracic Society Guideline for MPE. Thorax 2023;78 Suppl3. ATS 2018 Management of MPE

question_stem_truncated: Q18 about HFrEF CAD - 58yo new HFrEF EF 30% exertional chest pain CCS2, etiology workup most common cause
correct_answer: CAD is most common cause of HFrEF; invasive coronary angiography recommended if angina or high probability CAD
original_issue: CAD not listed error, non-ischemic only listed
corrected_guideline_title: ESC 2021 HFrEF Guidelines - EHJ
corrected_recommendation: ESC 2021 states CAD is most common cause of HFrEF; recommends non-invasive or invasive coronary assessment in patients with angina, high pre-test probability, or new HFrEF.
corrected_paper_title_authors_year: McDonagh TA et al. 2021 ESC Guidelines for Heart Failure. Eur Heart J 2021;42:3599-3726

question_stem_truncated: Q19 about early EN - 45yo septic shock intubated day 1 stable on norepi 0.08, lactate clearing, when to start EN
correct_answer: Early EN within 24-48h in hemodynamically stable critically ill on stable low-moderate vasopressor, trophic then advance
original_issue: EN timing error, delayed 7 days incorrectly
corrected_guideline_title: ASPEN 2022 Guideline for Nutrition Support in Critically Ill - JPEN
corrected_recommendation: ASPEN 2022 recommends early EN 24-48h in critically ill patients who are hemodynamically stable, even on low-moderate vasopressor, to preserve gut integrity and reduce infection.
corrected_paper_title_authors_year: Compher C et al. ASPEN Guideline for Nutrition Support in Critically Ill Adult. JPEN J Parenter Enteral Nutr 2022;46:12-41
